workshops.title: Profiling lab: connect a workload to trace and sample evidence
workshops.summary: Build a small instrumented UIKit app, check its shared workload on the Mac, and plan one controlled investigation. Keep raw records and separate synthetic arithmetic from device measurements.

simple.story: A cook times the work of making one bowl of soup. She starts when she begins preparing that bowl and stops when it is ready on the counter. Waiting for a free stove happened earlier. Carrying the bowl to the table happens later. Her timer answers how long the preparation took. It does not answer how long the guest waited. To compare another recipe, she must keep the bowl size and timing rule the same, and check that the soup is still correct.
simple.meaning: A profiling interval needs a defined start and end. Work spans worker entry through model preparation. It excludes queue delay, UI delivery, and presentation. Comparable records must share their workload and environment. The small numbers below are invented arithmetic practice, not observations.

example.before: Two valid synthetic variants each have three successful Work durations. Baseline values are 2, 4, 6 ms; candidate values are 1, 3, 5 ms. No phone ran these examples.
example.change: Sort each variant's values and select the middle value to compute its median.
example.after: The baseline median is 4 ms and the candidate median is 3 ms. That is a 1 ms difference in invented data. With only three successes per variant, the lab's twenty-success minimum is unmet; the record gate would report insufficient_samples.

picture.caption: The Work interval measures worker preparation and leaves other parts of the user wait outside it.

items.label: Queue wait
items.text: An accepted attempt can wait before worker entry; Work has not started.

items.label: Work starts
items.text: The worker begins model preparation and opens Work.

items.label: Model ready
items.text: Projection, decoding, disk verification, and wrapping finish, closing Work.

items.label: UI and display
items.text: Main delivery and presentation happen after Work and need separate evidence.

words.meaning: A named event or interval marker that lets a trace connect execution to a specific operation.
Records grouped under matching conditions so their comparison has a stated basis.
The middle sorted value, or the average of the two middle values when the count is even.
The sorted value at rank ceil(0.95 times the sample count), using ranks starting at one.
Profiler samples attributed to a function's own execution rather than its descendants.
A chain of strong ownership references that keeps an object alive.

simple.remember: Name the interval, check correctness, and keep invented numbers separate from measured records.
simple.boundary: Soup timing explains interval boundaries, not CPU sampling, asynchronous scheduling, or frames on screen. Work time is not total user wait. Synthetic arithmetic cannot prove a phone is faster, and twenty successes is a lab minimum rather than statistical confidence or release approval.

sections.title: Identify the app and what each evidence level supports
sections.html:
A native workload is work executed by an app built for Apple platform APIs. This lab connects a recording plan to that workload. MeasurementLab covers synthetic regression decisions; ProfilingLab supplies an app that projects records, decodes images, performs file I/O, and renders rows. Open ProfilingLab.xcodeproj and select the shared ProfilingLab scheme. App/ProfilingApp.swift contains the UIKit entry and controls. Core/Workload.swift is compiled by both the app and the host checker. The target has no company dependency or network request, and does not modify the production client.

The project declares iOS 17 and Swift language mode 5. Its Profile action uses Release, optimization and symbols. Signing is disabled for the checked-in scratch project; configure it in a learner-owned copy when you have authorized device access. Apple signposts require iOS 15 or macOS 12, independently of this target's deployment minimum. Host compilation requires an Apple toolchain with Foundation, ImageIO, CoreGraphics and os. The record scripts require Node with native ES modules and no downloaded dependencies.

List each evidence level in your notebook: source inspection, compiler build, executed host checks, native interaction, physical-device traces, and production review. A generic simulator artifact can be built without a working simulator runtime. This workshop records available verification in README and leaves unsupported levels pending. None of the supplied data marks learner work complete.

sections.title: Check the output and ownership before measuring time
sections.html:
A correctness check asks whether the workload produces the intended result. Run it before comparing speed. From the course directory, create a unique temporary output directory and follow the README's swiftc command. Compile Core/Workload.swift with Host/Checks.swift using the specified language mode, optimization, and module-cache path. Run the resulting host-checks binary with an isolated fixture-output path. A fixture is known input for a repeatable check. This checker compares both projection strategies with an independently expected ordered array, checks empty input, and interrupts each strategy at its second cancellation poll.

The same checker generates the square PNG, verifies 2048-square full output and 240-square thumbnail output, rejects a corrupt image and proves temporary JSON round-trip cleanup. ARC releases objects when their strong owners are gone. This test clears an external probe owner, observes the deliberate strong callback cycle, then clears callback and observes release. Its queue test suspends a one-worker queue, accepts four actions, requests cooperative cancellation and drains all terminal callbacks. This is a controlled schedule rather than a sleep-based race guess.

These checks establish mechanics on the host. They do not certify phone image quality, screen accessibility, memory ceiling, launch timing or energy. Kotlin/Java analogies help you reason about immutable fixtures, task outcomes and lifecycle ownership, but Swift ARC's cycle behavior and Apple image APIs are separate semantics. Preserve the output and actual tool versions rather than reporting that an iOS app ran because the shared core executed.

sections.title: Record one defined operation and keep other controls fixed
sections.html:
A signpost marks a named event or interval in a trace. Start with a repeatable input: Linear projection, Thumb image policy, Cached caption, and one worker. Prepare local fixture generates the synthetic PNG before Work. Begin an Instruments recording with os_signposts and Time Profiler, run one four-attempt batch, wait for pending zero, then stop and save. Record the process, effective configuration, destination identity, OS build, source revision, fixture, and preparation. If no runtime is available, prepare these coordinates and leave the observation fields blank. A ready plan is not an executed capture.

Work starts at worker entry and ends after model preparation: string construction, projection, decoding, file verification, and UIImage wrapping. It excludes queue delay, main delivery and presentation. Projection, Decode and Disk are nested intervals; ModelApplied is an event before reloadData. ShellConstruction is a root-window delegate subphase. Select one operation before reading its call tree, which groups functions by call path. Separate main and blocking-queue execution. Inclusive samples include descendants; self samples cover only the function's own execution. Array.contains descendants inside Projection support a membership hypothesis; a large whole-trace percentage does not.

Compare Indexed with the other controls frozen, check output first and collect a matched confirmation batch. For the separate caption experiment, populate the table before recording a fixed gesture and freeze projection, image and worker policy. Caption exists only for the repeated branch, so use a common hitch or responsiveness track to compare the two screen variants. A missing candidate span is an absent calculation, not a measured zero-duration frame.

sections.title: Follow image owners and work limits under pressure
sections.html:
A decoded image occupies memory for pixels, not just the compressed file bytes. Compare Full and Thumb while keeping projection, caption, and worker count fixed. Use the same prepared source. Record allocations created during Work and images that remain after the batch. The controller intentionally retains four successful images while displaying only the first. Clear displayed payload removes those owners after pending reaches zero. Pixel dimensions can support an estimated decoded-byte cost. Actual peak memory and the footprint after clearing still need observations; they cannot be inferred from the source alone.

A retaining path is a chain of strong references keeping an object alive. Use Create callback cycle, release its external owner, and follow RetentionProbe's strong closure capture in a stopped Memory Graph. The weak witness is only an observer. Resume, break the callback cycle and repeat the ownership check. Allocation generations show surviving populations; a Memory Graph shows ownership at an instant. An autorelease pool cannot fix this cycle, and a garbage-collector analogy cannot substitute for ARC edge reasoning.

Worker capacity limits how much accepted work can execute at once. Comparing one versus four workers is a separate scheduling experiment. The backlog remains four attempts, and lowering active capacity does not revoke decoders already executing. Required work reduces to one under serious pressure or Low Power Mode; the host-testable speculative branch declines optional work, but the app has no prefetch producer. Thermal endpoints and admission snapshots do not capture a full pressure history. Phone energy and sustained thermal behavior require supported device tooling; this local workload supplies no radio savings evidence.

sections.title: Keep original attempts and annotate a separate copy
sections.html:
Provenance records where a result came from. Export raw JSON only after the batch drains, and keep the original file. Records retain completion append order and a separate admission ordinal, which numbers attempts when admitted. The app labels its source native-unannotated and leaves environment fields blank. Add real recording coordinates to a separate copy before validation. Do not relabel native data synthetic to bypass missing device identity or revision. Worker outcome and elapsed time end before UI delivery. A late cancellation can therefore suppress publication after a worker success record already exists.

For deterministic arithmetic practice, run Records/make-synthetic.mjs into the temporary directory and validate that generated file. The synthetic records deliberately have blank device and OS fields. The validator checks identity, provenance, finite duration, correct success output, stable pressure, prepared fixtures and one revision per variant. It groups cohorts, meaning records with matching comparison conditions, before computing median and nearest-rank p95. It keeps failed attempts and refuses to make a release decision. Run Records/checks.mjs for timeout, cancellation, corruption of metadata, mixed revision, pressure drift and incorrect-output cases.

The generated baseline has twenty successful values from eighty to ninety-nine and the candidate from seventy to eighty-nine. Their medians are 89.5 and 79.5, and p95 values 98 and 88. These are invented fixture values verified by arithmetic, never phone observations. review_required means descriptive input readiness. invalid_capture, correctness_failure and insufficient_samples demand different next actions, and the original failed records remain audit evidence.

sections.title: Give the reviewer evidence, a budget, and a recovery plan
sections.html:
An evidence packet contains the files and coordinates another person needs to check a claim. Retain source, commands, tool versions, fixture, original and annotated records, validator report, matching binary/symbols, and selected trace coordinates. Name the user budget, correctness requirements, acceptable failure limits, reviewer, and rollback. For example, faster worker completion is not enough if output changes or UI delivery regresses. A source complexity argument can motivate a candidate. A regression decision still needs representative confirmation under comparable conditions and an owner who can reverse the change.

A simulator comparison remains its own cohort. A successful unsigned build, host dimension check or synthetic p95 cannot become a device launch, smoothness, memory or energy result. When hardware is absent, the concrete completed deliverable is the target, host behavior, raw tooling and a ready-to-execute recording plan. Leave native interaction, allocation paths, phone samples, pressure history and operational review explicitly pending.

exercise.brief: Build the scratch target and run its host and record checks. Choose one controlled native investigation, then perform it or document exactly what remains pending.
steps: Create a unique temporary directory. Run the README's build and host commands and save the results.
Generate the synthetic raw file, validate it, and run the checks that deliberately alter records. Keep the synthetic label.
Choose one native change to compare. Hold the other controls fixed and define the recording interval before capture.
Package the obtained evidence and the recording plan. Use separate rows for pending native interaction and device measurements.
acceptance: All shared-core and raw mutation checks pass using isolated outputs.
The target builds for the declared SDK/configuration or an exact blocker is recorded.
The investigation defines signpost boundaries, variant, fixture, failure denominator and artifact paths.
Synthetic values remain labeled; no native/device measurement is claimed without its artifact.
exercise.solution:
Compile the shared workload and run the host gates. Save the output for ordered projection parity, controlled cancellation, full and thumbnail dimensions, corrupt-image rejection, file cleanup, and callback lifetime. Keep the result for all four queued cancellation callbacks reaching their terminal paths. The separate Release app build checks target wiring. It does not run the screen. The raw-record checks verify arithmetic on invented data, retain timeout counts, and reject invalid successes, mixed revisions, pressure drift, and incorrect output. Each result supports a specific claim; none becomes a phone measurement merely because the same source is compiled into an iOS app.

The worked investigation chooses Linear versus Indexed with Thumb, Cached caption and one worker fixed. Image preparation occurs before capture. Work is worker-entry-to-model-ready; the note explicitly excludes accepted-tap queue delay and presentation. The recording plan adds os_signposts and Time Profiler, selects one Projection child, and compares descendant/self attribution. Stack and timing observations remain blank until the learner saves a trace. A separate minimally instrumented batch supplies confirmation; no predicted saving is written as a measured result.

For an obtained native export, preserve the original and annotate a copy from actual device/OS/revision/configuration evidence. The validator report is attached alongside all failed and cancelled attempts. A final review names the budget owner and recovery if the isolated candidate regresses. If the runtime or hardware is unavailable, the packet states that build and host checks passed while launch, gesture, allocation graph, sustained pressure and energy remain pending. This answer demonstrates a substantial reproducible workflow without pre-completing a learner capture or a production decision.

quiz.question: Which evidence level does executing Host/Checks establish?
options: Shared-core correctness and ownership behavior on the host
quiz.explanation: The checker runs actual Apple host code and verifies specific mechanics. It does not interact with the iOS screen or measure phone resource behavior.

quiz.question: Why keep the original native-unannotated export?
options: It preserves original provenance while annotations are added to a reviewable copy
It can be relabeled synthetic to avoid missing device fields
quiz.explanation: Annotations must come from obtained recording evidence. Retaining the original makes that change auditable and prevents fabricated environment claims.

quiz.question: What should you compare after reducing caption calculation?
options: The absent candidate Caption span as a zero frame time
A common responsiveness/hitch metric under the same gesture plus behavioral parity
quiz.explanation: The asymmetric span explains removed work; the shared screen metric establishes whether that work affected responsiveness.
